records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ErrorEvent.timestamp defaults to 0.0 when the nodestore payload lacks a timestamp (data.get("timestamp", 0.0)), and gen_request_data sorts by that timestamp and compares it against event.get("timestamp", 0), so missing-timestamp errors sort to the very front of the log and are emitted before all breadcrumbs regardless of when they occurred. Users of the breadcrumbs summarization feature get error context positioned at the wrong point in the timeline, degrading the Seer summary's chronology with no error surfaced.
records.rationale: Verified in diff: `fetch_error_details` constructs `ErrorEvent` with `timestamp=data.get("timestamp", 0.0)` (src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py). Then `get_request_data` sorts `error_events` by `timestamp`, and `gen_request_data` emits any error whose timestamp is `< event.get("timestamp", 0)` before yielding breadcrumb messages. Therefore an error missing `timestamp` will default to `0.0`, sort to the front, and be emitted before all breadcrumbs regardless of actual chronology, matching the finding.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The reports array is validated and accepted with no bound on the number of reports per request or the size of each report body (body is an unbounded DictField), so a single POST can submit an arbitrarily large batch that is fully deserialized, logged via logger.info with the entire request_body, and validated report-by-report before returning 200. The collector endpoint (permission_classes = (), CSRF-exempt, CORS-enabled) is an unbounded-ingestion path: a browser or script can push huge report arrays that inflate log volume and memory on the request path, with no cap and no rate limit.
records.rationale: In `BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint.post`, the request body is fully deserialized (`request.data`) and logged verbatim (`logger.info("browser_report_received", extra={"request_body": request.data})`), and then every element of `raw_data` is validated in a loop with `BrowserReportSerializer(data=report)` / `is_valid()`. There is no bound on `raw_data` length and `body` is `serializers.DictField()` (unbounded), so a single unauthenticated, CSRF-exempt, CORS-enabled POST (`permission_classes = ()`, `@csrf_exempt`, `@allow_cors_options`) can submit an arbitrarily large array and/or large bodies,
